claim: rumqttc 0.24.0's set_clean_session(true) removes all state from queues and instructs the broker to clean all client state on disconnect; false makes the broker hold state, and local queue state is also held to retransmit packets after reconnection — and it panics if clean_session=false is set with an empty client_id.
stance_target: The ha-linux-agent (on rumqttc 0.24.0) can implement persistent sessions with broker-side queueing across its own restarts, but must always set an explicit client_id or the client panics.
scope_conditions: rumqttc 0.24.0 (exact Cargo.lock-pinned version), MQTT v3.1.1 session semantics
quoted_support: clean_session = true removes all the state from queues & instructs the broker to clean all the client state when client disconnects. When set false, broker will hold the client state and performs pending operations on the client when reconnection with same client_id happens. Local queue state is also held to retransmit packets after reconnection. ... Panics if clean_session is false when client_id is empty.

claim: MqttOptions 0.24.0 exposes set_keep_alive (ping when no other data exchange), set_last_will(LastWill), set_request_channel_capacity, set_pending_throttle (outgoing message rate), set_inflight(u16) (concurrent in-flight), set_max_packet_size(incoming, outgoing), set_manual_acks — there is no MQTT5 clean-start/session-expiry API on this version.
stance_target: The supervisor spec must be buildable from the pinned 0.24.0 API surface: LWT at connect, keepalive, and inflight/throttle knobs exist; MQTT5 session-expiry features do NOT exist in the pinned version.
quoted_support: set_keep_alive — Set number of seconds after which client should ping the broker if there is no other data exchange ... set_pending_throttle — Enables throttling and sets outoing message rate to the specified 'rate' ... set_inflight — Set number of concurrent in flight messages

claim: rumqttc 0.24.0 claims automatic reconnection by just continuing the eventloop.poll()/connection.iter() loop, natural backpressure to client APIs during bad networks, half-open-connection detection via pings, and queue-size-based flow control — but outgoing throttling is still a TODO.
stance_target: The supervisor does not need to hand-roll reconnect loops: it must keep polling the eventloop; but blocking inside the poll loop halts all connection progress, so supervisor logic must run off the poll task.
quoted_support: Automatic reconnections by just continuing the eventloop.poll()/connection.iter() loop. Natural backpressure to client APIs during bad network. ... Looping on connection.iter()/eventloop.poll() is necessary to run the event loop and make progress. Blocking inside the connection.iter()/eventloop.poll() loop will block connection progress.

claim: The externally-polled eventloop gives users access to internal state for graceful shutdown or modifying options before reconnection, and rumqttc 0.24.0 re-exports mqttbytes v5 (MQTT5 packet encoding exists) even though MqttOptions is v4-centric.
stance_target: A supervisor can detect reconnect cycles via poll notifications and rewrite MqttOptions between connections; MQTT5 message expiry/session expiry would require a rumqttc upgrade or direct mqttbytes v5 usage, not the 0.24.0 MqttOptions API.
quoted_support: Since the eventloop is externally polled (with iter()/poll() in a loop) out side the library and Eventloop is accessible, users can ... Access internal state for use cases like graceful shutdown or to modify options before reconnection ... Modules§ mqttbytes mqttbytes v5

claim: rumqttc state.rs confirms the reconnect requeue mechanism: clean() returns all unacked outgoing QoS 1/2 publishes and pending PubRels as a Vec<Request> for the eventloop to requeue, while clearing incoming QoS 2 dedup sets and resetting ping/collision counters — and the design comment says the same state should be kept for persistent sessions but a new state instantiated for clean sessions.
stance_target: On connection loss the agent's unacked QoS 1 publishes are not lost: rumqttc re-buffers them and retransmits after reconnection (matching the MqttOptions 'local queue state is also held' doc), so the supervisor's job is to re-establish subscriptions and re-publish retained state, not to re-send every telemetry message.
scope_conditions: rumqttc state.rs at bytebeamio/rumqtt main (0.24.x-era architecture)
quoted_support: Returns inflight outgoing packets and clears internal queues ... Creates new mqtt state. Same state should be used during a connection for persistent sessions while new state should be instantiated for clean sessions

claim: In state.rs, outgoing_subscribe() unconditionally assigns a packet id and returns a Subscribe packet — it does NOT itself buffer subscribes pre-connection; buffering happens in the eventloop's request channel above it, and unsolicited acks error out while pkid collisions park publishes until CollisionTimeout at 2 pings.
stance_target: Whether client.subscribe() before the first connect is safe: safe in rumqttc because the request sits in the bounded flume channel until the eventloop first connects and drains it — but the request channel capacity (Client::new(options, cap)) bounds how much pre-connect enqueueing is possible.
scope_conditions: rumqttc state.rs at main; state layer only
quoted_support: fn outgoing_subscribe(...) { let pkid = self.next_pkid(); subscription.pkid = pkid; ... Ok(Some(Packet::Subscribe(subscription))) } — no pre-connection buffering at this layer
